title: Ennin's travels in Tang China
summary: The Japanese monk Ennin sailed to China in 838 with the last official Japanese embassy to the Tang court, was shipwrecked near the coast, then travelled via Yangzhou and Mount Wutai to the capital Chang'an. He saw Buddhism suppressed there and returned to Japan in 847 with a diary and scriptures.

uncertainty.note: The pages disagree on some years: the Mount Wutai visit is put in 840 (Wilson's map), 'the following year' after 838 (Encyclopedia.com), and spring, 'presumably 839' (World History Encyclopedia, which says the Yangzhou, winter and Wutai years are inferred); the persecution is given as 841-846 (Wilson) and 845 (World History Encyclopedia). The route is plotted through the three named places with the years as stated by Wilson and Encyclopedia.com.

importance.justification: The route of the last official Japanese embassy's monk, whose day-by-day diary is one of the major accounts of Tang China and of the 9th-century suppression of Buddhism.

beats.caption: Ennin travels to China with the last Japanese embassy to the Tang court; the ship is wrecked and he comes ashore safely.
He spends about two months at the pilgrimage site of Mount Wutai, then goes to the capital, where he studies for years.
After the suppression of Buddhism he finds a ship home in 847, carrying scriptures and the diary of his journey.

reviewer_note: Least sure: year of the Wutai visit (839 vs 840) and of the persecution; the route has no stop between Chang'an and the return port because none of the opened pages names one. Yangzhou year is the landing year from the map caption plus a page naming Yangzhou. Wikidata points are city or mountain centres.
